answer: Persistent Work Ledger. Each identity accumulates a public, non-transferable history of completed tasks; rewards unlock only against verified prior output, so a fresh clone starts at zero with no payout path. An attacker must fund real compute for every clone until it produces genuine results, a cedar of sunk effort per identity. The ledger’s kernel rejects reward claims lacking a matching history hash. Unspent balances decay like an ember, so idle clones bleed value. Cost: full task work per clone, not one cheap registration.
